title: Operations on complex analytic functions
statement: Let $E,F,G$ be finite-dimensional [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] normed complex vector spaces. Here analytic at a point means represented on a neighbourhood by a convergent complex power series. A constant map is analytic at every point, and a continuous complex-linear map $E\to F$ is analytic at every point. For maps $u,v:E\to\mathbf C$ analytic at $a$, $u+v$ and $uv$ are analytic at $a$; if $u(a)\ne0$, $1/u$ is analytic at $a$. If $f:E\to F$ is analytic at $a$ and $g:F\to G$ is analytic at $f(a)$, then $g\circ f$ is analytic at $a$. A map analytic at $a$ is continuous at $a$. For any finite index set $J$ and maps $f_j:E\to\mathbf C$ analytic at $a$, the tuple $x\mapsto(f_j(x))_{j\in J}$ is analytic at $a$.
